newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates steady as market remains tight.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates steady as market remains tight.

text.p: Interbank rates were steady on Thursday as the market remained tight and commercial banks continued to cover short positions, dealers said.

"Rates are pretty much the same this morning. Some commercial banks are still short and Bank Negara is believed to be still lending one-month money at eight percent," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.

Maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 500 million ringgit on Friday in addition to the one-billion ringgit bill issue which matured on Wednesday should help improve market liquidity, though not for long, dealers said.
They said there will be an outflow of around two billion ringgit on June 26 due to maturity of funds which Bank Negara lent to the market to help ease a liquidity squeeze last month.
One-week money was at 7.80 percent against 7.70/80 percent on Wednesday.
One- and three-month money were steady at 7.8/8.0 percent.
The overnight rate, which traded between 6.0 and 7.8 percent on Wednesday, was expected at 7.0-8.0 percent.
"A couple of big commercial banks are still short on the overnight," said one dealer.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were higher on expectations of easing interest rates following news of a slower growth in money supply in April, futures market dealers said.
Bank Negara said on Wednesday broad money M3 grew by 19.7 percent in April against 21.0 percent in March.
At 0300 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) December contract was up two points to 92.66, or an implied yield of 7.34 percent.
March and June 1998 contracts both rose three to 92.72, or 7.28 percent.
